 One possibility is that S. started work on the poem some time, and perhaps soon, after
Jane’s birthday on 21 January, with a conception involving the gift of an instrument, and
the idea of the spirit Ariel reincarnated in S.’s body. Subsequently, on hearing from Smith
by early March that no harp would be coming from Paris, S. proceeded in March to buy a
guitar locally (Trelawny claimed to have accompanied S. to Leghorn to make the purchase;
see Rossetti 1870 ii 576), and to develop the related image of a tree-spirit reincarnated in a
guitar made from the wood of the tree, incorporating new knowledge of the construction
of the guitar from pine. As Mary’s account of Jane having access only to ‘a very bad piano’
is in a letter dated 5 March, the gift, together with its poem, must have been presented after
